senses.en_definition: Because; owing to. Indonesian form of standard Malaysian Malay kerana.

messages.en: In that Indonesian drama, the character says 'karena aku sayang kamu'. Does karena mean 'because', like sebab?
Yep, that's right. Indonesian uses karena, while standard Malay in Malaysia uses kerana. In everyday conversation, we usually just say sebab.
This tabletop's still a bit rough. It needs a little more sanding.
I've already bought some sandpaper. We can sand it together in a bit.

senses.en_definition: Love or deep affection for someone or something.
To love or feel affection for someone.

collocations.en: to tell; to let someone know

senses.en_definition: (Colloquial) To let or allow; to refrain from preventing.
(Colloquial) To cause something to be or become a certain way.

messages.en: Got my wallet! Thanks for dropping it off earlier. I'd have had trouble going out tomorrow without it.
No problem. I was passing through your neighbourhood anyway. Good thing you noticed it was missing so soon.
Coffee's on me tomorrow, and don't you say no!

collocations.en: to feel sorry for someone on seeing their plight

messages.en: I feel sorry for Hakim. He's been looking after his mum at the hospital for two days now.
Poor guy. Let's take him some food so it'll be easier for him to grab a bite later.
